To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PIAS1, the SUMO ligase, functions as a target selective AR coregulator on chromatin to modulate the prostate cancer cell transcriptome.

PIAS1 is required for the expression of a subset of androgen-regulated genes in prostate cancer cells, and that it functions as a target-selective coregulator for AR by modulating AR chromatin occupancy and gene regulation.
PIAS1 is required for the expression of a subset of the androgen-regulatory genes and for the androgen-induced cell growth in prostate cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of novel transcriptional coregulators of the androgen receptor (AR), a nuclear receptor that regulates gene transcription in response to the androgen testosterone and plays a key role in the development of the prostate and in the progression of prostate cancer (PCa).
the role of PIAS1 in the regulation of gene expression by AR in prostate cancer.
the molecular mechanisms of androgen-regulated gene expression in prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SUMO E3 ligase PIAS 1 is a genuine AR coregulator in prostate cancer cells, which regulates a subset of AR-regulated genes in a target gene specific fashion and also masks distinct genomic loci to androgen regulation.
PIAS1 is required for androgen-regulated transcription and prostate cancer cell growth and that PIAS1 regulates AR activity in a gene-selective manner.
PIAS1 is not a general AR coregulator but rather a specific one that is required for the expression of a subset of AR target genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PIAS1 is involved in the androgen-regulation of prostate cancer cell proliferation through the control of a subset of AR target genes and the exposure of a new set of AR-regulated genes.
PIAS1 is the first androgen receptor (AR)-interacting SUMO ligase identified and it is a genuine AR chromatin-bound coactivator.
PIAS1 is overexpressed in human prostate cancer and it is a target gene selective AR coregulator in the VCaP cell line.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PIAS1 is not a general AR coregulator, but a selective one that regulates a specific subset of AR target genes.
PIAS1 is not only involved in the regulation of androgen receptor (AR)-mediated transcription but also in the regulation of the androgen receptor itself.
SUMO ligase PIASA1 functions as a chromatin-bound coregulator that regulates the androgen receptor transcriptional activity in a target gene-selective fashion.
